You are reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary as a BLACK BOX. The C++ library source is NOT available and you must NOT look for it.

Binary: /workspace/dataset/test20_executable
Invoke: /workspace/dataset/test20_executable '<word>'      (exactly one argument)
It prints exactly 20 lines to stdout, one per API call, in this fixed order (1-indexed):
  1  pluralize(word)
  2  singularize(word)
  3  camelize(word)                       // default 2nd param
  4  camelize(word, false)
  5  underscore(word)
  6  classify(word)
  7  tableize(word)
  8  humanize(word)
  9  titleize(word)
  10 dasherize(word)
  11 parameterize(word)
  12 parameterize("A " + word + " Test")
  13 upcase(word)
  14 downcase(word)
  15 capitalize(word)
  16 decapitalize(word)
  17 truncate(word, 5)
  18 demodulize("Test::" + word)
  19 to_string(isPlural(word))    -> "0"/"1"
  20 to_string(isSingular(word))  -> "0"/"1"

With no argument it prints nothing. With an empty argument it ABORTS (std::out_of_range from
basic_string::substr inside demodulize) printing nothing to stdout.

TOOLING TIPS
- Extract one line:  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable 'word' | sed -n '5p'
- Show exact bytes:  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable 'word' | sed -n '5p' | od -c
- Loop:  for w in a b c; do printf '%s -> ' "$w"; /workspace/dataset/test20_executable "$w" | sed -n '5p'; done
- Use $'...' bash quoting for control bytes / high bytes, e.g. $'a\tb', $'\xc3\xa9'.
- 'file' is unavailable; 'strings', 'od', 'sed', 'nl' work.
- The binary is fast; run HUNDREDS of probes. Be exhaustive, not economical.

GROUND RULES
- Every claim in your output MUST be backed by an observed probe you actually ran.
- Assume C locale: toupper/tolower/isalnum/isspace behave as ASCII-only; bytes >= 0x80 are
  unchanged by case ops and are NOT alnum. VERIFY this rather than assuming.
- Note operations are byte-based (std::string), not char-based. Test multi-byte UTF-8.
- Report the algorithm as precise pseudocode that a Rust programmer can transcribe with zero guessing,
  operating on BYTES.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (underscore_dasherize):
Characterize line 5 underscore(word) and line 10 dasherize(word).
underscore hypothesis: for i,c in bytes: if isupper(c) && i>0 { push '_' } ; push tolower(c).
  Verify with: HelloWorld, ADMIN, aB, "Hello World", "Foo::Bar", "A", "AB", "aBC", "A1B",
  "-A", "_A", leading uppercase, consecutive uppercase runs, digits adjacent to uppercase,
  UTF-8 bytes adjacent to uppercase, and whether '-' is ever converted to '_'.
  Also check whether it de-duplicates underscores ("a_B" -> "a__b"?) and whether the i>0 test is
  positional or "previous char was not already an underscore".
dasherize hypothesis: replace every '_' byte with '-'. Verify it does nothing else (spaces,
  existing dashes, case, UTF-8).

content.text: All probes complete. Hypotheses confirmed exactly, with two testing artifacts identified and resolved (byte `0x0A` breaks line-splitting — resolved by full `od -c` dump; a trailing `':'` aborts the whole program in line 18 `demodulize`, so no stdout at all).

apis.name: underscore
apis.pseudocode:
underscore(input: bytes) -> bytes:
    out = empty byte buffer
    for i in 0 .. len(input)-1:
        c = input[i]
        if c >= 0x41 ('A') and c <= 0x5A ('Z'):
            if i > 0:
                out.push(0x5F '_')          # PURELY POSITIONAL test on the index i,
                                            # NOT "previous byte was not '_'" and NOT
                                            # "previous byte was lowercase/alnum".
            out.push(c + 0x20)              # ASCII tolower
        else:
            out.push(c)                     # every other byte copied verbatim
    return out

NOTES (all observed):
  * Only bytes 0x41..0x5A are treated as uppercase. Bytes >= 0x80 (Latin-1 / UTF-8
    continuation & lead bytes) are NEVER lowercased and NEVER trigger a '_'.
    (C locale confirmed by exhaustive sweep of bytes 0x01..0xFF.)
  * NO de-duplication of '_': an existing '_' before an uppercase letter still gets
    another '_' inserted.
  * '-' is NEVER converted to '_'.  ' ', '\t', '.', '/', ':' etc. are all left alone.
  * '::' is NOT converted to '/' (unlike Rails' ActiveSupport underscore).
  * Digits are not special: a digit before an uppercase letter still gets a '_'
    inserted, and an uppercase letter before a digit does not.
  * Output length is between len(input) and 2*len(input).
  * Byte-based, not char-based: a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence followed by an ASCII
    uppercase letter gets '_' inserted between them.

evidence.output: \xc3\xa9_a  ('é_a' — '_' inserted between the multi-byte seq and 'a')
\xc3\x89  ('É' unchanged — high bytes are NOT lowercased, C locale)

evidence.input: a\nB  (embedded LF, read via full `od -c` dump)
evidence.output: a\n_b  (LF is just an ordinary non-uppercase byte)

evidence.input: exhaustive sweep: every byte 0x01..0xFF placed in contexts <b>, <b>z, Z<b>, <b>A, _<b>, a<b>z (1530 inputs)
evidence.output: 0 deviations from the model (excluding the 0x0A line-splitting artifact and the 0x3A trailing-colon program abort, both separately explained)

evidence.input: 600 randomized byte strings (len 1..12) over alnum + punctuation + control + high bytes, seed 42
evidence.output: 594 usable cases, 0 mismatches vs the model

edge_cases: Empty input is untestable: the program aborts (std::out_of_range from substr in line 18 demodulize) before any stdout is flushed. Logically the loop body never runs, so underscore("") == "".
Single uppercase letter gets NO leading underscore: "A" -> "a", "X" -> "x" (the i>0 guard).

The i>0 guard is strictly positional. "_A" -> "__a" and "a_B" -> "a__b" prove there is no "skip if previous byte is already '_'" de-duplication, and "-A" -> "-_a" proves '-' does not suppress insertion either.
'-' is never rewritten to '_': "kebab-case" -> "kebab-case", "a-B" -> "a-_b".
'::' is preserved literally, NOT turned into '/': "Foo::Bar" -> "foo::_bar".
Consecutive uppercase runs are fully exploded, one '_' per letter (no acronym handling): "HTMLParser" -> "h_t_m_l_parser", "URLValue" -> "u_r_l_value".
Digits are ordinary: "9A" -> "9_a" (underscore inserted after a digit), "A9" -> "a9" (none before a digit).
Whitespace is preserved verbatim and does not suppress the underscore: "Hello World" -> "hello _world" (note the space AND the underscore), "a\tB" -> "a\t_b", "  A" -> "  _a".
Bytes >= 0x80 are inert: never case-folded, never trigger '_' themselves, but DO count as a position so a following ASCII uppercase gets '_' ("\xc3\xa9A" -> "\xc3\xa9_a").
Multi-byte UTF-8 uppercase letters (É U+00C9, Ω U+03A9) come out unchanged — confirms C locale / ASCII-only toupper-tolower.
Control bytes 0x01..0x1F (incl. LF 0x0A, CR 0x0D, VT 0x0B, FF 0x0C) and DEL 0x7F are copied verbatim and count as positions.
NUL (0x00) is not testable through argv.

Any input whose LAST byte is ':' makes the whole program abort (line 18 demodulize does substr past the end), so line 5 is not directly observable for those; ':' in every other position behaves as an ordinary byte.
Output can be up to 2x the input length (all-uppercase input), so pre-allocate 2*len.

apis.name: dasherize
apis.pseudocode:
dasherize(input: bytes) -> bytes:
    out = copy of input
    for i in 0 .. len(out)-1:
        if out[i] == 0x5F ('_'):
            out[i] = 0x2D ('-')
    return out

That is the ENTIRE operation: a 1:1 in-place byte substitution of '_' -> '-'.
Explicitly verified to do NOTHING else:
  * length is always exactly preserved (no insertions, no deletions)
  * case is NOT changed ("A_B" -> "A-B", "Hello_World" -> "Hello-World")
  * spaces / tabs / newlines / other punctuation are untouched ("a b" -> "a b")
  * pre-existing '-' bytes are left alone, NOT collapsed or de-duplicated
    ("a__b" -> "a--b", "_-_" -> "---")
  * leading and trailing '_' are converted like any other ("_leading" -> "-leading",
    "trailing_" -> "trailing-")
  * bytes >= 0x80 pass through untouched; the substitution is byte-wise so it can
    never corrupt a UTF-8 sequence (0x5F never appears inside a multi-byte sequence)

evidence.input: a\nB  (embedded LF, read via full `od -c` dump)
exhaustive sweep: every byte 0x01..0xFF in contexts <b>, <b>z, Z<b>, <b>A, _<b> (1275 inputs)
evidence.output: 0 deviations from pure '_'->'-' substitution (excluding the 0x0A line-splitting artifact and the 0x3A trailing-colon abort)

evidence.input: 600 randomized byte strings (len 1..12) over alnum + punctuation + control + high bytes, seed 42
evidence.output: 594 usable cases, 0 mismatches vs the model

edge_cases: Empty input untestable directly (program aborts in line 18 demodulize before flushing stdout); logically dasherize("") == "".
Output length always equals input length exactly — verified on the 400-byte "a_"x200 case and by the exhaustive byte sweep.
NO underscore de-duplication or collapsing: "a__b" -> "a--b", "__" -> "--".
Pre-existing '-' bytes are not touched and not merged with newly produced ones: "_-_" -> "---", "a_b-c_d" -> "a-b-c-d".
Leading/trailing underscores are converted, producing leading/trailing dashes; there is no trimming: "_leading" -> "-leading", "trailing_" -> "trailing-".
Case is completely untouched (this is NOT underscore-then-dasherize): "HelloWorld" -> "HelloWorld", "A_B" -> "A-B".
Whitespace (space, tab, LF, CR) is untouched — dasherize does NOT convert spaces to dashes (contrast with parameterize on line 11/12).
All bytes >= 0x80 pass through byte-identical; since 0x5F cannot appear inside a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence, the substitution is always UTF-8 safe.
NUL (0x00) not testable through argv.
Inputs ending in ':' abort the whole program (line 18), so line 10 is not directly observable for those; ':' elsewhere is untouched ("a:b" -> "a:b", "Foo::Bar" -> "Foo::Bar").

uncertainties: Inputs whose LAST byte is ':' cannot be probed at all: line 18 demodulize("Test::" + word) throws std::out_of_range (`basic_string::substr: __pos (which is 8) > this->size() (which is 7)` for word=":") and the process aborts with rc=134 before stdout is flushed, so lines 5 and 10 produce no output. ':' in every non-final position was verified to be an ordinary inert byte, so I am confident (but did not directly observe) that a trailing ':' is also inert for underscore/dasherize.

The NUL byte (0x00) cannot be passed through argv, so its behavior in underscore/dasherize is unobservable. Both functions iterate over std::string length, so NUL would be an ordinary inert byte, but this is inference, not observation.
Empty-string behavior is unobservable for the same abort reason. Both models degenerate to the identity on an empty byte slice.

Inputs containing LF (0x0A) desynchronize naive `sed -n '5p'` line extraction. I resolved this by dumping the complete 36-line output of `a
B` with `od -c` and locating the 5th and 10th API results by position; both matched the model (underscore -> "a
_b", dasherize -> "a
B"). Automated sweeps still flag 0x0A as an artifact.

I did not test inputs longer than 600 bytes, so I cannot rule out some pathological large-input branch, though the 600-byte alternating-case case scaled exactly as the model predicts (900-byte output).

Locale was not explicitly manipulated (no LC_ALL/LANG override probes). All observed behavior is consistent with the C locale: every byte in 0x80..0xFF, including Latin-1 uppercase 0xC0..0xDE, was left uncased and never triggered an underscore.
